questions.q: Which system in the vehicle is responsible for transmitting rotation from the engine to the wheels?
options: Power transmission — clutch, gearbox and differential
The suspension system
The steering system
The brake system
questions.explain: Power transmission (the clutch, the gearbox and the differential) transmits rotation from the engine to the wheels at the rate suited to the vehicle’s speed.

questions.q: What is the chassis’s role in the vehicle?
options: To serve as a rigid base for the vehicle and to crumple in a controlled way in a crash
To supply electricity to the vehicle’s systems
To absorb bumps in the road
To cool the engine
questions.explain: The chassis carries the body, the engine and every other system, and is designed so that certain areas of it crumple in a crash to absorb energy.

questions.q: Which system keeps the tyres in constant contact with the road, even over bumps?
options: The suspension system
The exhaust system
The cooling system
The gearbox
questions.explain: The suspension system absorbs bumps and keeps the tyres in contact with the road, which is essential for steering and braking.

questions.q: What is the most useful way to start diagnosing a new fault or noise in the vehicle?
options: First identify which system the fault belongs to — engine, brakes, steering and so on
Turn off all the panel’s warning lights
Try to ignore it and keep driving as usual
Replace all the tyres immediately
questions.explain: Identifying the system involved is the first step in diagnosing a fault, and it also helps you describe it correctly to the garage.

questions.q: How many pedals does an automatic vehicle have, and which foot is used for them?
options: Two pedals — brake and accelerator — both with the right foot only
Three pedals, right foot for the accelerator and left foot for the brake
Just one pedal that combines accelerator and brake
Two pedals, both operated with the left foot
questions.explain: An automatic vehicle has no clutch pedal. There is only the brake and the accelerator, and both are operated in turn with the right foot only.

questions.q: What is the parking brake’s role?
options: To shorten the braking distance at high speed
To steer the front wheels
To change gear without a clutch
To hold the vehicle in place even when the engine is off
questions.explain: The parking brake — a lever, an electric button or a separate pedal — is meant to hold the vehicle in place while stationary, not for an emergency stop while driving.

questions.q: In an automatic vehicle, which gear-lever position is for normal forward driving?
options: R
P
D
N
questions.explain: D (Drive) is the position for driving forward. P is for parking, N for neutral and R for reverse.

questions.q: What is usually on the stalks on either side of the steering wheel?
options: Turn signal and lights on one side, wipers and washer spray on the other
The parking brake and the clutch
The fuel gauge and the rev counter
Just the ignition button
questions.explain: Usually one stalk is used for the turn signal and for switching between dipped and main beam, and the other for the wipers and spraying washer fluid.

questions.q: Why is it recommended to learn the location of all the controls in an unfamiliar vehicle before your first drive in it, rather than hunting for them while driving?
options: Because the controls differ in every vehicle and can’t be learned in advance
Because the law forbids touching the controls while driving
Because hunting for a control distracts you from the road at exactly the moment a fast reaction is needed
There’s no special reason — it’s purely a matter of comfort
questions.explain: Hunting for a control such as the wipers or the turn signal while driving takes your eyes and your attention off the road, at exactly the moment a fast reaction might be needed.

questions.q: What is the correct headrest height?
options: Its top level with the crown of the head
Level with the shoulders
The height doesn’t matter, only the angle
Level with the lower back of the neck
questions.explain: A headrest that’s too low doesn’t support the neck in a rear-end collision and can make whiplash injury worse. The correct height: the top level with the crown of the head.

questions.q: Where should the lap part of the seatbelt run?
options: Low across the pelvis
Under the arm
Behind the back
High across the stomach
questions.explain: The lap belt should run low across the pelvis, not the stomach — so it doesn’t cause internal injury under braking or in a crash.

questions.q: How should the side mirrors be adjusted correctly to shrink the blind spot?
options: So that you mainly see the vehicle’s own rear door
As close as possible to the centre of the vehicle
There’s no way to shrink the blind spot using mirrors
Very wide — until you see only a small edge of the vehicle in the corner of the mirror
questions.explain: A wide adjustment, until only a small edge of the vehicle is visible in the corner of the mirror, reduces the overlap with the rearview mirror and shrinks the blind spot.

questions.q: The mirrors are correctly adjusted. Do you still need to look over your shoulder before changing lanes?
options: Yes — a small blind spot remains that the mirrors don’t cover
No, the mirrors are always enough
Only at low speed
Only in an old vehicle without a rearview mirror
questions.explain: Even with the mirrors correctly adjusted, a small blind spot remains. A quick look over your shoulder is an essential part of the safety check before changing lanes.

questions.q: What is the correct seating position behind the steering wheel?
options: A seat reclined all the way back for comfort
The distance doesn’t matter, only the seat height
A distance that lets you press the brake all the way down with the knee slightly bent, and hands on the steering wheel with the elbows bent
A seat as far as possible from the steering wheel, to give the legs room
questions.explain: The right distance allows you to press the brake fully with the knee slightly bent, and to hold the steering wheel with the elbows bent — giving full control even in an emergency stop.

questions.q: When is the right time to check the engine oil and coolant levels?
options: It makes no difference whether the engine is hot or cold
Right after driving, while the engine is hot
Only when a warning light comes on
When the engine is cold, before you start driving
questions.explain: When the engine is hot, the oil hasn’t fully drained back into the sump yet, and the coolant may be boiling and under pressure. The correct check is with the engine cold.

questions.q: Where do you check the coolant level?
options: In the clear expansion tank
Directly under the radiator cap, at any time
On the oil dipstick
There’s no way to check it yourself — that’s the garage’s job alone
questions.explain: The coolant level is checked in the clear expansion tank, between the marked lines. The radiator cap itself is opened only when the engine is completely cold, and not for a routine check.

questions.q: What do you check in a walk-round of the vehicle before driving?
options: Only the seatbelts
Only the fuel level
The condition of the tyres by eye, that the lights are intact, leaks under the vehicle, and clean glass
Only the tyre pressure, with a precise gauge
questions.explain: The walk-round is a quick visual check: the condition of the tyres, intact lights, no fresh fluid stain under the vehicle, and clean, undamaged glass.

questions.q: Why must you never open the radiator cap or the expansion tank while the engine is hot?
options: The fluid is boiling and under pressure and can cause serious burns
The cap locks automatically and can’t be opened
There’s no risk at all, it’s just an unnecessary recommendation
It will stop the vehicle from starting
questions.explain: The coolant in a hot system is boiling and under pressure. Opening the cap releases it all at once and can cause serious burns.

questions.q: What’s normal to see on the instrument panel the moment you start the engine?
options: No light should come on at all
All the warning lights come on briefly and then go out
Only one light should stay on permanently
All the lights should stay on for the whole drive
questions.explain: On starting, all the warning lights come on briefly as the system’s self-test, and then go out. A light that stays on needs looking into.

questions.q: What must you make sure of before starting a vehicle with a manual gearbox?
options: That the air conditioning is running at full power
That the window is open
That a high gear is engaged
That the clutch pedal is pressed all the way down
questions.explain: In most manual vehicles, the engine can only be started when the clutch pedal is pressed all the way down — this protects against the vehicle lurching forward when it starts.

questions.q: In an automatic vehicle, what position should the gear lever be in when starting the engine?
options: D only
The lever position doesn’t matter
R always
P or N, with a foot on the brake
questions.explain: In an automatic vehicle, you start the engine with the gear lever in P or N and a foot on the brake — that way the vehicle doesn’t move the moment it starts.

questions.q: Before reversing, what’s the safe way to make sure the way behind is clear?
options: Look directly behind you, not just in the mirrors
Rely on the side mirrors alone
No need to check if the engine is already running
Rely on the rearview mirror alone
questions.explain: Before reverse gear, come to a complete stop and look directly behind you — not just in the mirrors — because there could be a low obstacle the mirrors don’t show.

questions.q: Why is it important to apply the parking brake even when the vehicle is in P (automatic) or in gear (manual) when stopped on a slope?
options: It’s not necessary — the gear alone is always enough
Because without the parking brake the vehicle could shift slightly or roll on the slope
Because it saves fuel
Because the law forbids using the gear alone
questions.explain: A gear or position P limits the wheels’ rotation, but is not a full substitute for the parking brake, especially on a slope — so you use both together.

questions.q: What does central locking let you do in a vehicle?
options: Lock only the driver’s door
Lock all the doors in a single action, usually by pressing the remote
Lock only the boot
Switch off the engine remotely
questions.explain: Central locking locks (and usually also unlocks) all the vehicle’s doors together, usually with a single press of the remote or a switch on the door.

questions.q: Before opening the driver’s door and getting out of the vehicle, what should you look at?
options: The side mirror and behind you — a cyclist or motorcyclist could pass right there
Only ahead
There’s no need to look anywhere
Only at the fuel gauge
questions.explain: Looking at the side mirror and behind you before opening the door prevents hitting a cyclist or motorcyclist passing by the vehicle.
